Start with the space. We recommend a thirty-six by sixty-nine foot footprint. That leaves room for the ring beam the court anchors into, comfortable access, machinery during installation, and good gameplay.

Headline: THE CONCRETE SLAB
Dimension labels: 36' X 69' (11M X 21M)
Area label: 2,484 SQ FT (231 M²)
Cross-section labels: 6" POST-TENSIONED · 4,000 PSI · PITCHED 0.5-1%
Caption: BUILT TO DRAIN
Sub-caption: 6-inch post-tensioned slab, at least 4,000 PSI

That footprint is your concrete slab: thirty-six by sixty-nine feet, about twenty-five hundred square feet. We build it six inches thick, post-tensioned, at least four thousand PSI, and pitched slightly so water runs off. Skip this and you'll see cracking, ponding, and turf failures.

Confirm: slab = full 36' x 69' (Sergio's quote uses 2,484 SF). Slope: the page says 0.5-1%, you've said 0.5-0.7% is best. The FSC brochure shows a rebar slab, not post-tensioned. Video will match the page unless you change it.

Headline: ORIENTATION
Compass: N · S
Caption: OUTDOORS: RUN IT NORTH-SOUTH
Sub-caption: Keeps the low sun out of players' eyes
Outdoors, run the court's long axis north-south. East-west works, but the sun sits in players' eyes at sunrise and sunset.
Side view of the full court; ceiling lines draw above.

Top: AMERICAN PADEL LABS
Headline: INDOORS
Labels: COMPETITION: 23'-26'3" (7-8M) · MIN. CEILING 19'8" (6M)
Under diagram: SIDE VIEW, FULL COURT
Caption: 19'8" OF CLEAR HEIGHT
Sub-caption: 6m minimum above the whole playing surface
Building indoors? You need at least nineteen feet eight of clear ceiling. Twenty-three feet for club play, twenty-six feet three for competition. Lights, ducts, and beams all go above that.
